predictive_observations: RugCheck flagged 'Large Amount of LP Unlocked' as danger, with 0% LP locked in one of the top markets. Liquidity that the deployer can withdraw is the direct way a pair ends up with 'no pair or no liquidity' at T_D.

A sibling clone from the same launch window (DdAQ..., created about 6 minutes earlier) had already done $1.68M of 1-hour volume and had only $71.43 of liquidity left. Several other same-name tokens showed $0 liquidity. That is a live example of the drain pattern in the same cluster, visible at T2.
GMGN showed creator_token_status = creator_close and 17 creator launches (21 via the dev's X account). A serial deployer who has already exited fits a pull-and-relaunch pattern.

GMGN created_unix equals migrated_unix (1790231836) on meteora_virtual_curve, so there was no organic bonding-curve phase. The pool was effectively seeded straight away, which suggests the deployer supplied the liquidity and controls it.
Extreme h1 turnover (about 110x liquidity) together with -78% to -81% five-minute price moves is consistent with a liquidity event already under way, not ordinary trading.
The report's p_rug of 62 and strong_fade view pointed the right way. No position could be opened, so this call is only weakly confirmed.
misleading_observations: GMGN lp_burn_ratio = 1.0 contradicted RugCheck's unlocked-LP flag. If the outcome was a liquidity pull, the burn figure was the wrong one to trust (likely stale or measured on a different pool). The report correctly marked the two sources as conflicting and did not resolve it.

Reading 2,097 unique buyers against 94 unique sellers as volume cycling is plausible, but GeckoTerminal's unique-trader counts on brand-new pools are unreliable. The outcome does not test this interpretation.
The 'fading volume' point came from a partial 5-minute candle. That is weak evidence, and the frozen outcome does not show whether it mattered.
The counterargument that volatility makes a +100% touch possible did not matter in the end. The trade could not be filled, so bracket dynamics never came into play.
Only 6 GMGN page visits was read as low human attention. That fits the result but is not what made the trade unfillable.
The ATH near $1.3M mcap said nothing about whether liquidity would survive the next 22 minutes.
evidence_that_should_have_changed_conclu: The conclusion was already negative, so nothing needed to reverse it. The drained sibling clone plus unlocked LP plus creator_close was strong enough to justify an explicit near-term warning that the pair might not exist or be fillable at T_D. The report treated rug risk only over the 6-hour window and never called out the 22-minute gap between T2 and T_D.

At research time the report saw liquidity of about $57k and a -61% five-minute move. When LP is unlocked and a sibling has already drained, a live liquidity check close to T_D would have been the relevant step. The report does not show any timing awareness.
Some caution: 'unfillable' could also come from a data or API gap, not a confirmed rug. The outcome record does not say which. So hindsight should not claim the rug was certain.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: If a target token belongs to a same-name/same-ticker cluster launched within about 15 minutes, and at least one sibling had over $500k of 1-hour volume but now has under $1k of liquidity, then the target is much more likely than the base rate to have no fillable liquidity within 30 minutes of T2.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Cluster of 5 or more same-name tokens created within 15 minutes of each other. Target has non-pump.fun-curve liquidity. Measured using only the same_ticker_or_name_tokens data at T2.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Clone clusters are usually run by one operator who seeds liquidity, farms volume, then pulls liquidity pool by pool. A sibling that has already been drained shows the operator's playbook and timing directly.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: Tokens where created_unix equals migrated_unix on a non-pump.fun launchpad (such as meteora_virtual_curve), together with a RugCheck 'LP unlocked' danger flag, have a higher rate of becoming unfillable or dropping over 90% by T_D than migrated tokens that went through a real curve phase.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: GMGN launchpad is not pump.fun. Created and migrated timestamps are within 60 seconds. RugCheck reports at least one top market with under 10% LP locked. Apply even when GMGN lp_burn_ratio says 1.0.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Skipping the curve phase means the deployer supplied the pool liquidity directly, so the LP tokens stay withdrawable. Curve graduation normally burns or locks LP by protocol.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: For candidates with h1 turnover above 50x liquidity and a creator_close status from a creator with 10 or more prior launches, the chance that liquidity falls over 80% between T2 and T_D (about 20 minutes) is materially above the experiment's base rate.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Assessed at T2 from GMGN dev fields and trigger turnover. Outcome measured as liquidity at T_D compared with liquidity at T2.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Serial deployers who have already closed their creator position and are running wash-level turnover are extracting value on short cycles. Liquidity removal is their exit, and it tends to come within minutes, not hours.

structured_output.summary: The trade was never filled because there was no pair or no liquidity at 07:52, about 22 minutes after T2 and after the research fetch that showed about $57k of liquidity. The most likely explanation is that the deployer pulled liquidity, but the record does not confirm this; a data gap cannot be ruled out. The report's negative view (strong_fade, p_rug 62) pointed the right way, and its reasoning about a serial deployer, unlocked LP, a clone cluster and no narrative was sound. The strongest evidence available at the time was structural. RugCheck flagged unlocked LP. A sibling clone had already been drained to $71 after $1.68M of volume. GMGN showed creator_close with 17 launches. The token was created and migrated at the same instant, suggesting deployer-seeded liquidity. The report's weakness was framing: it treated rug risk over a 6-hour trade window instead of the short gap between T2 and T_D. It also left the conflict between lp_burn_ratio 1.0 and RugCheck's unlocked flag unresolved, and the burn figure turned out to be the misleading one. The buyer/seller asymmetry, the partial-candle 'fade' and the counterargument about volatility did not bear on the outcome. With one unfillable case, this confirms little. Treat the call as reasonable reasoning with a directionally right result, not as proof.
